subject: economics
title: Equilibrium Adventure
welcome_lead: Where supply meets demand — that's the magic price. ⚖️
meta_desc: Supply & Demand Basics Adventure 3 — KS3 Economics on market equilibrium and price changes.
final_note: You learned what equilibrium is, what surpluses and shortages look like.

concepts.def: Too much supply at this price
Too little supply at this price
A change moving the whole curve

walkthroughs.body_html:
Where the supply curve crosses the demand curve = equilibrium.

Buyers want the same amount that sellers offer. Nice and balanced.

If price is too high → surplus (unsold items piling up). Sellers drop prices.

If price is too low → shortage (empty shelves). Prices rise.

Markets keep correcting themselves.

A new trend pushes the demand curve right → higher equilibrium price.

New tech pushes the supply curve right → lower equilibrium price.

Real markets shift every day. 📊

mcqs.q: What defines a pure public good?
options: A recession is when the stock market crashes.
Non-rivalry (one person's use doesn't reduce others') and non-excludability (you can't stop people benefiting) — e.g. national defence, street lighting.
A public good is anything that's free.
A public good is anything provided by the government.

mcqs.q: What is the technical definition of a recession?
options: PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
A recession is when the stock market crashes.
Two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth — a contraction of the economy.
A recession is when prices fall and people lose jobs.

mcqs.q: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
options: PED measures how flexible or stretchy a product is.
PED measures whether a product is expensive or cheap.
A recession is when the stock market crashes.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price — the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price.
